name: Empathic Reactions (EMNLP 2018)

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.scope: Dataset text and numeric ratings; excludes third-party article/reading-material full texts.

empathy.instruction: Estimate the reaction writer's self-reported empathic concern on the published scale from 1 (low) to 7 (high).
empathy.field_description: essay: Original English reaction essay written after reading a news story; the news article itself is not included.

distress.instruction: Estimate the reaction writer's self-reported personal distress on the published scale from 1 (low) to 7 (high).
distress.field_description: essay: Original English reaction essay written after reading a news story; the news article itself is not included.

field_descriptions.essay: Original English reaction essay written after reading a news story; the news article itself is not included.

text_policy: Original selected text and capitalization preserved byte-for-byte after UTF-8/CSV decoding; grouping uses a separate whitespace-normalized casefolded hash. No spelling correction, truncation, label imputation, or score transformation.
grouping_rule: Connected components of source response_id and whitespace-normalized casefolded essay. response_id is a questionnaire response/session key, not a verified permanent participant identifier. Both targets share the same group.
split_policy: No new fixed split imposed. Future splits must hold out entire groups jointly across both targets. Repeated article IDs are preserved in source_refs for a separate article-disjoint evaluation; response grouping alone does not enforce article independence.
source_citation: Buechel, Buffone, Slaff, Ungar and Sedoc (2018), Modeling Empathy and Distress in Reaction to News Stories, https://aclanthology.org/D18-1507/
quality_findings: Two separately supervised tasks are generated from each valid reaction; the other target and binary label fields are always excluded from input.
Labels measure the writer self-reported state and are not an objective external measure of empathy.
Only reaction essays are redistributed; no news articles fetched.

checks: All retained labels finite and within documented rating scale
Every retained input and label compared with its original decoded CSV/TSV row
Every source row accounted for; invalid/missing labels never imputed
Explicit input allowlists exclude source IDs, other scores, bins, demographics and article full texts
Official splits retained; cross-split identical inputs and connected groups counted and flagged
Source version, downloaded bytes and SHA256 recorded

deduplication_rule: Same task, normalized input, normalized label AND official split; preserve all source_refs. Across-split copies retained and flagged, same-input dependencies unioned. Different labels retained.
sample_id_rule: sha256([task_id,input_hash,label,split]) first 24 hex; official split included to preserve split occurrences.
